content:
Hello! In 2024, I discovered a kernel optimization that I applied to the Lean4Lean kernel, which made it 22% faster in typechecking mathlib, I opened this PR for it where you can see how it works -- basically, it reuses free variable names where possible so that we get more cache hits when defeq-checking.

I recently got around porting it to the actual Lean kernel in this commit, and I have also benchmarked it and it seems to also deliver some gains there, making mathlib typechecking 16% faster (2.2 minutes saved total).

Is this something that would be worth opening a PR for? It is a kernel change but it seems fairly safe to do, in my opinion. I might also try porting this optimization to the elaborator to see if it also speeds things up there.

I'm not part of the FRO, so I can't say whether this would be a welcome change, but I think it would be interesting to see how much speedup this optimization gives when applied to the elaborator. I've heard this idea before, of reusing fvars, but I don't think anyone has implemented it before.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

I've heard this idea before, of reusing fvars, but I don't think anyone has implemented it before.

IIRC Trepplein did this, and the implementations using deBruijn levels kind of do it by design. It might be an issue in lean4lean if it changes the verification conditions by requiring some additional lemmas about the caching being sound.

I'm guessing changing the elaborator would require some changes to the API and/or careful reviewing of where the mk_reused_fvar_name equivalent would need to be called. In particular, it's very easy, and probably done a fair bit in the elaborator, to change a local decl of a lctx to transform it from a lambda/forall-bind cdecl to a let-bound ldecl, which would break the invariants needed for such a cache to function correctly. I don't see why such things would happen in the kernel, though this would also need to be reviewed if this change was to be merged there. In any case, I believe fvar reuse would be nice to have.

Do you get any additional performance gain from also having an equivalent reuse for let-bound fvars ? This would require adding another map like m_fvar_type_to_reused_name except from a pair of (type, value) to fvarIds, and an equivalent mk_reused_fvar_name function, but might be very useful in let-heavy contexts.

Arthur Adjedj said:

Do you get any additional performance gain from also having an equivalent reuse for let-bound fvars ? This would require adding another map like m_fvar_type_to_reused_name except from a pair of (type, value) to fvarIds, and an equivalent mk_reused_fvar_name function, but might be very useful in let-heavy contexts.

I benchmarked it, there's essentially no benefit for let fvar reuse across mathlib, I think that they're used too infrequently for it speed things up at all. But perhaps it could help with a library that does use them a lot.
